import pandas as pd

# List all source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_4.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_5.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_6.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_7.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_8.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/test_9.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and types
target_columns = ['admit', 'gre', 'gpa', 'prestige']
target_dtypes = {
    'admit': int,
    'gre': int,
    'gpa': float,
    'prestige': int
}

# Step 1: Load all source tables into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    # Read CSV with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0)
    # Ensure columns are exactly the target columns (all sources have same schema)
    df = df[target_columns]
    dfs.append(df)

# Step 2: Concatenate all source DataFrames (UNION operation)
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Step 3: Enforce target data types
combined_df = combined_df.astype(target_dtypes)

# Step 4: Save the combined DataFrame to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length9_10/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
